headline: Acorn CCS cluster left in funding limbo after UK Budget reprioritises its £200m grant
summary: The £200m of CCS capital grant pulled in the Autumn Budget was earmarked for Acorn in north-east Scotland; the project has had no confirmed lead developer since Storegga stepped back (Dec 2025), and the Treasury says the commitment stands but may convert to loans or equity.
source: Scottish Construction Now / energy-pedia / ITV News
co2crc_note: A flagship 'Track-2' cluster destabilised by fiscal reprioritisation — a cautionary case on grant-dependent CCS funding models relevant to Australian CCS hub financing.
extractor_note: Same £200m reprioritisation as item #03 (policy); amount recorded on the policy item to avoid double-counting. Government says commitment stands (possible loans/equity), so status is at-risk rather than firmly cancelled.

headline: Ozona and Marubeni reach FID on Pawnee carbon-sequestration project in Texas
summary: Ozona CCS and Japan's Marubeni took a final investment decision on the Pawnee project, a 50:50 JV in Bee County, Texas (Eagle Ford), with Ozona building and operating storage and Marubeni leading carbon-credit commercialisation; capacity and capex were not disclosed in the reports seen.
co2crc_note: Trading-house-led offtake/commercialisation model (Marubeni) for US onshore storage — a commercial template of mild interest for CCS value-chain structuring.
extractor_note: FID confirmed across trade press; no Mtpa or capex figure disclosed in sources seen (WebFetch blocked this run).

headline: UK Autumn Budget pulls £200m from carbon-capture grants; Viking kept, Acorn hit
summary: The 28 October Budget reprioritised £200m of CCS capital grants to defence (trade press framing it as part of a ~£700m cut across CCUS and hydrogen), maintained the Viking (Humber) grant, kept Track-1 Teesside/HyNet/North Wales as priorities, and signalled a possible move from grants to loans/equity.
source: The Chemical Engineer / Carbon Brief / Energy Voice
co2crc_note: A major Western government cooling public CCS grant support — directly relevant to how Australian CCS programmes read political/fiscal risk to capture-hub subsidies.
extractor_note: NEGATIVE funding event: £200m of CCS-specific grant WITHDRAWN/reprioritised (not new money). The ~£700m figure is CCUS+hydrogen combined (not CCS-only) and is not recorded as the amount. Government says it stands by the commitment and may convert to loans/equity.

headline: UK and Taiwan launch CCUS cooperation partnership
summary: The UK and Taiwan launched a CCUS partnership to share policy, regulatory and supply-chain experience, pairing the UK's cluster track record with Taiwan's new carbon-storage regulation (Aug 2026) and state-utility demonstrations; scope and funding were not detailed.
co2crc_note: Bilateral UK-APAC CCUS cooperation; Taiwan is an under-covered emerging storage market and a potential APAC CCS collaboration node of interest to CO2CRC.

headline: 'Gravest betrayal': Scotland reacts angrily to Acorn CCS treatment in the Budget
summary: Scottish business and political figures branded the reprioritisation of Acorn's £200m an 'abject betrayal' of north-east Scotland's carbon-capture ambitions, with the Deputy First Minister demanding clarity from Westminster — a CCS social-licence flashpoint over walked-back public funding.
co2crc_note: Social-licence lesson: visible public/political backlash follows a government walking back CCS funding — reputational risk relevant wherever CCS relies on public subsidy.
extractor_note: Media/social-licence reaction to the same Budget event as items #01 and #03.
